You are the **orchestrator** for Wondarr (Windows, `D:\Code\wondarr`). Read first: `AGENTS.md`, `docs/HANDOVER.md` (especially §7 Session log, the build-session-7 entry), `docs/build/PROGRESS.md` (Phase 6), `docs/build/PHASES.md` (Phase 7), `docs/build/AGENT_WORKFLOW.md`, `docs/build/CODING_STANDARDS.md`, `docs/build/MODEL_VALUE_MATRIX.md`; skim `docs/DECISIONS.md` (build session 7) and consult `docs/architecture/*.md` per task. They are binding.

**Goal:** Phase 7 — qBittorrent and SABnzbd sources — to its "done when" gate: a song only available inside an album torrent is imported by downloading just that file; an NZB album downloads, unpacks, and only the wanted track(s) are imported; two wanted songs from the same album are satisfied by one grab. Scope (from `PHASES.md`): a Torznab/Newznab SourceProvider (ported from Lidarr: per-indexer `caps`, `t=music` vs `q=` fallback, categories, Prowlarr endpoints; recording → releases (MusicBrainz) → release searches; release-name quality parsing; `.torrent` metainfo file listing; container-file matching by track number/title/size), the qBittorrent client (add stopped, `stopCondition=MetadataReceived`, `files`, `filePrio`, `start`, 4.x/5.x states, categories, remote path mappings, completion by wanted files, import by file index), the SABnzbd client (whole post, post-unpack track selection), bundling (other wanted songs in the same container from one grab). `release/push` (Phase 5) should then accept torrents and NZBs. Start by writing `docs/build/PHASE_7_TASKS.md` (research first: qBittorrent's current WebUI API v2 for 4.x/5.x, SABnzbd's API, Prowlarr's Torznab endpoints, and the licence/attribution of every Lidarr file you port — `NOTICE.md`); the handover's first three tasks are P7-01 the Torznab/Newznab provider, P7-02 the qBittorrent client with file selection, P7-03 the container-file matcher and import by file index.

**Pre-flight (one short report):** toolchain; `.env` presence (never print values; read them with `worker.py`'s loader); CI green on `main` (Phases 0–6 together, 2026-10-07 — the Phase 6 stage needs `tests/gate/replay`; when a gate's songs change, record with the manual **Record gate metadata** workflow and commit its artifact); the OpenRouter key's remaining limit (USD 26.46 of 30 used after build session 8, about USD 3.54 left — enough for about three T3 worker runs; ask the owner to raise it before P7-03b/P7-06 if more is needed); the live instance on `ch01` (http://ch01.ad.wulff.com.au:1077, `develop` image) is up; `python scripts/test_worker_agent.py` passes; run `/openrouter-value` to refresh `docs/build/MODEL_VALUE_MATRIX.md` and note which tier picks changed. Phase 7 needs test instances: qBittorrent (5.x) and SABnzbd containers on `ch01` (or fakes in FakeSlskd for CI, as Phase 6 faked Plex) — ask the owner for Prowlarr/indexer access only if a live check needs real indexers. Lessons from build session 7 (`PROGRESS.md` "Phase 6"): command handlers resolve far-reaching services in a scope per run; never run a merge while a worker tests; workers cannot regenerate the OpenAPI snapshot (do it at merge); T3 workers ran out of turns on every M-sized backend task — size Phase 7's tasks smaller or expect to finish them.

**Per task:** spec from `WORKER_TASK_TEMPLATE.md` (state its tier) → commit the spec → `WONDARR_WORKER_BASE=<your base branch> python -u scripts/worker.py --model <tier pick> run docs/build/tasks/<id>.md` in the background **with a background timeout above `WONDARR_WORKER_TIMEOUT_MIN`** → review adversarially and run the builds, tests and frontend checks yourself → the reviewer (`worker.py review`, T3 pick) for anything touching processes, files, time, the database, auth or external limits → fix the findings yourself when that is cheaper than a continuation → merge only through `scripts/safe-merge.sh` → update `PROGRESS.md`, docs, `NOTICE.md`, the OpenAPI snapshot and the frontend types (regenerate them *after* merging the base into a branch; regenerate a branch's migration when another migration merged first) → Conventional Commit, no model names, no AI trailer → push to `main`. Phase 4 workers regularly stopped at the turn cap with work uncommitted: set `WONDARR_WORKER_MAX_TURNS=100` for T2/T3 tasks, and expect to finish, test and commit the remainder yourself.

**Verification beyond unit tests:** the upgrade gate is end to end: import an MP3-320 song under a profile whose cutoff is FLAC, make a FLAC appear on the (fake) Soulseek, run the UpgradeSearch, and check the old file is recycled, the new file verified and imported, history says "upgraded", and Plex sees one file (the throwaway-Plex recipe is in `PROGRESS.md` "Phase 3 gate"). Test the race: a Compact staging a song's file while an upgrade lands for the same song. Backup: take a backup on a populated instance, restore it into a fresh container, and compare settings, songs, history and the API key behaviour. External-slskd mode: run `scripts/phase2-gate.py` against it unchanged. A live check on `ch01` before calling anything done. Before big test runs kill stale `testhost` processes (check command lines first; keep MSBuild nodes, the NuGet MCP server and csdevkit), always build after adding a new test file (`dotnet test --no-build` ignores it), and never run three suites at once on a loaded machine.

**Rules:** everything in `AGENTS.md` "Non-negotiables" (never write `.webm`, never produce lossless from lossy, a transcoded YouTube file keeps quality `OPUS-160`; an upgrade never replaces a file with a worse one); never merge red; workers never touch `AGENTS.md`, `CLAUDE.md`, `docs/DECISIONS.md`, `docs/adr/`, `.claude/`, `.github/workflows/`, `.env*`. Stop and ask me only for (a) a decision that would change an ADR, (b) spend beyond the budget, (c) a blocker outside the repo. Otherwise decide, record it in `PROGRESS.md`/`DECISIONS.md`, and continue.

**Model selection for every delegated call (workers, reviewers, researchers, API single-shots):** do not default to the `.env` pin. Choose per task by effort tier from `docs/build/MODEL_VALUE_MATRIX.md` ("Tier picks"). Match the tier to the task spec, take the matrix's cheapest model that clears that tier's minimum scores, and pass it with `python scripts/worker.py --model <id> run|api|review ...`:

- **T1 mechanical** (port or transform a file, boilerplate tests, doc drafts) → `worker.py api`, the T1 pick.
- **T2 standard** (ordinary feature or test work in a worktree) → T2 pick.
- **T3 hard** (touches processes, files, time, the database, auth or external limits) and **every reviewer run** → T3 pick.
- Escalate one tier after a failed continuation (bounded to 2 rounds, as in `AGENT_WORKFLOW.md`) instead of retrying the same model; take over yourself after T3 fails.
- Use the **"Cheapest at list price"** column for anything that must keep working for the whole session (a promo can expire mid-run); the "now" column is fine for short one-off tasks. Run `/openrouter-value` at the start of the session, again whenever the matrix is more than 7 days old, and whenever a model id is rejected or a worker under-performs; then re-pick (it needs `openrouter.ai` reachable; the command wraps `python scripts/openrouter_value.py --out docs/build/MODEL_VALUE_MATRIX.md`).
- Log the tier and model id in each task's `PROGRESS.md` line with the real cost (`.worker/<id>/runs.jsonl`), so the next session can see whether a tier's pick is under-performing and move its floor up.

**Style:** a status line when you start each task, one paragraph after each merge, no narration in between.

**Done for this session:** Phase 7's tasks merged and its gate demonstrated (CI with fakes — a torrent client and an indexer answering from fixtures, an NZB post — and live on `ch01` against real qBittorrent/SABnzbd containers), `PROGRESS.md`'s Phase 7 section with costs, and a dated `docs/HANDOVER.md` Session log entry with the first three Phase 8 tasks (`PHASES.md`). If you run out of time or budget first, write the handover entry anyway and push.
